Correction lands; sole NM track, reviewed in full. Reason is exact and single-cause — the route is not bound into the filing-assembly system — and it is honest that the loss is LegalEase's typing rather than the participant's access, since the Supreme Court publishes the amended forms free. Mechanism is correct and unusually well-bounded: NMSA 1978 Section 29-3A-3 petition where identity theft produced the record; on a showing the court SHALL order expungement and cause delivery to all relevant law enforcement agencies and courts; a civil district-court petition even where the underlying case was municipal, magistrate or metropolitan and even where no case was ever filed; Rule 1-077.1 supplies the procedure and makes Form 4-951 mandatory; service of the petition not required under Rule 1-077.1(E). Destination is exact — the New Mexico district court for the county where the charges originated, where the arrest occurred, or where a conviction was entered, verbatim from Rule 1-077.1(B)(1) as the brief carries it, with the Supreme Court Form 4-951 URL from officialSources[1]. Every fact traces to the brief: $132.00 district court filing fee, usually money order or cashier's check, Form 4-222 in its place; ~$0.35 per page for court copies; Forms 4-951 and 4-960.1 in the versions approved 31 October 2025; Supreme Court Order No. S-1-RCR-2024-00099 effective for cases pending or filed on or after 31 December 2025; no waiting period; the post-order timing rules (minimum sixty days to complete, no court-record expungement earlier than thirty days from entry, and the civil expungement proceeding itself must be expunged); Section 29-3A-2(A) and 29-3A-2(C) carve-outs including the authorized-background-check category; no reach to federal, tribal, military or out-of-state records; FINRA/SEC employment disclosure surviving; records not destroyed outside the cannabis and DNA provisions; the Judiciary's direction that non-citizens seek advice. The due-process rule is handled exactly right and is the treatment's strongest element: never name the person you believe used your identity, anywhere in the petition or the proposed order, with the reason given (Rule 1-077.1 deliberately omits the Section 29-3A-3(D) true-offender insertion; the committee commentary explains that naming without notice would violate due process). No required component silently optionalised — mandatory Form 4-951 is stated as mandatory and signed by the participant; 4-960.1, the order and 4-222 are presented consistently with their conditional status; the manual-completion boundaries (hearing date/time/location blank, caption only on the order) are stated in both the doNot list and nextSteps. The treatment openly states the unresolved limitation that New Mexico publishes no list of acceptable identity-theft proof, and still gives the exact destination and next step ('bring everything you have', plus Find a Case and the clerk's docket/arrest sheet) — correct under the standard, not a defect. Spanish is genuine translation at a participant register throughout, not a gloss: 'robo de identidad', 'giro postal o cheque de caja', 'encabezado', 'debido proceso', 'exoneración de la tarifa', 'despacho asistido por computadora', 'libros de registro de los equipos de prueba de alcohol en el aliento'; every en/es pair differs and every list length matches. Briefcase preserved/outstanding/return complete, ending 'Guarda la vía; no guarda una petición'. No prohibited phrase in either language; no packet promise.
